title: I3C target (SDR framing on the two-wire base): START / STOP detection, 7-bit address 0x2A, ACK, bytes both ways, an in-band interrupt request after each write

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Byte returned to the controller on reads

fields.desc: sent MSB first for every byte of a read, until the controller NACKs; read bit by bit as the byte goes out (the MSB at the SCL fall ending the address or the previous ACK), so change it only between a byte's last bit and the ACK clock that follows

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Bytes written by the controller (acknowledged); reading RX frees it

fields.desc: addressed: between our address and the STOP or the NACK
IBI request, active low: set by the STOP that ends a write, released by the next START

irqs.name: BYTE
irqs.desc: a byte was received (the same clock RX captures it)

notes: sda (open drain: the target only pulls it low) and scl are the bus pins; they pass through unchanged. SCL and SDA are sampled on PCLK, so each SCL phase must last at least three PCLK clocks.
The address is the core parameter I3C_ADDR (0x2A). Another address is ignored until the next START or STOP. Dynamic addressing, CCCs, HDR modes and the IBI arbitration on SDA are not implemented.
